title: Leakage-Controlled TinyML IDS Experimental Pipeline
primary_message: The study is an end-to-end, leakage-aware and deployment-oriented TinyML IDS workflow.

title: Leave-One-Device-Out Generalization
visual_form: device-level grouped point or bar chart
primary_message: Neural TinyML models retain strong performance under strict device holdout.

title: Compression Accuracy and Resource Trade-off
visual_form: Pareto scatter with model size or latency against Macro-F1
primary_message: P50-QAT provides a favorable TinyML deployment trade-off.

title: Final Model-Family Pareto Selection
primary_message: The final family was chosen from multi-objective deployment evidence, not test-metric ranking of checkpoints.

title: Input Perturbation Robustness
primary_message: TinyML models are substantially more stable than HGB under noise and scale drift.

title: Dataset, Split, Leakage-Control, and Evaluation Protocol
primary_message: Evaluation follows locked, leakage-aware and test-isolated protocols.

title: Classical Baseline Performance
primary_message: HGB is the strongest clean-data classical baseline but is not the most robust.

title: Five-Seed Compression Results
visual_form: mean, standard deviation, weighted Macro-F1, size, and fragility table
primary_message: QAT preserves accuracy better than post-training dynamic quantization.

title: CPU Deployment Benchmark Results
visual_form: latency, throughput, size, parameter, and MAC comparison table
primary_message: The selected static-INT8 family reduces resource demand while retaining accuracy.

title: Omnibus and Post-hoc Statistical Results
primary_message: Global differences are detectable, while five-seed pairwise resolution remains limited.

title: Input Robustness Results
primary_message: HGB has five severe fragility cases; TinyML models have none.

title: Reproducibility and Release Artifacts
primary_message: The selected deployment package is independently verified and reproducibly locked.
